summary: This regulation explains the rules for a listed company that wants to do a scheme of arrangement, such as a merger or a plan handled by a court. The company must first file the draft plan with the stock exchange and pay a fee to get a No-objection letter. It cannot file the plan with a court or tribunal until it receives this letter.
points: The listed entity must file the draft scheme of arrangement along with a non-refundable fee with the stock exchange to get a No-objection letter before filing with any Court or Tribunal.
The listed entity must not file any scheme of arrangement with any Court or Tribunal unless it has obtained the No-objection letter from the stock exchange.
The listed entity must place the No-objection letter before the Court or Tribunal when seeking approval of the scheme.
The listed entity must submit prescribed documents to the stock exchange after the Court or Tribunal sanctions the scheme.
The listed entity must ensure compliance with other requirements prescribed by the Board from time to time.
example: Sunrise Industries Limited, a company whose shares are traded on the stock market, plans to enter into a scheme of arrangement. Before taking this plan to a tribunal, Sunrise Industries Limited must file a draft of the scheme with the stock exchange along with the required fee. The company must wait to get a No-objection letter from the stock exchange. Once the letter is issued, Sunrise Industries Limited can then present both the scheme and the No-objection letter to the tribunal for approval.

terms.meaning: A court-approved plan between a company and its creditors or shareholders, such as a merger or restructuring.
An official body or authority appointed to deal with legal cases and disputes.
A formal letter stating that the stock exchange does not oppose the proposed plan.
A company that has its securities listed and traded on a recognized stock exchange.

watch: Make sure to obtain the No-objection letter from the stock exchange before submitting the scheme to any court or tribunal.
